chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Amr ibn Bakr, from Jabir, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever recites all of the Musabbihat (the seven short surahs starting with Tasbih) before sleeping will not die until he sees Al-Qa'im (peace be upon him), and if he dies, he will be in the neighborhood of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْقَائِمَ: Al-Qa'im, a title for the 12th Imam, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, who will rise to establish justice.
key_terms.الْمُسَبَّحَاتِ: The seven short surahs in the Quran that begin with the word 'Tasbih' (Surah Al-Hashr, Al-Saff, Al-Jumu'ah, At-Tahrim, At-Talaq, At-Tahrim, Al-Mulk).
key_terms.جِوَارِ: Neighborhood or proximity, indicating a high status of closeness to the Prophet in the afterlife.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting the Musabbihat before sleeping?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) links the nightly recitation of the 'Musabbihat'—the seven surahs beginning with glorification—to the eschatological hope of witnessing the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him). This practice not only secures a place in the spiritual neighborhood of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for those who pass away before the Qiyah, but also serves as a means of spiritual preparation and divine protection during the period of occultation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) said, “One who recites all the recommendations before going to bed will not die until he sees Qaim-e-Aale Muhammad (s.a.w.s.) and if he dies he will  get  place  in  the  neighborhood  of  the  Holy  Prophet (s.a.w.s.).”
